title: Polynomial-time randomized error reduction
statement: Suppose a language $L$ has a polynomial-time randomized verifier with polynomially many random bits, perfect rejection on inputs outside $L$, and acceptance probability at least $\min(2/3,(|x|+1)^{-c})$ on each input $x\in L$, for some natural number $c$. Then, for every natural number $d$, it has a polynomial-time randomized verifier with polynomially many random bits, perfect rejection outside $L$, and acceptance probability at least $1-2^{-((|x|+1)^d+1)}$ on every $x\in L$.
hypotheses_covered: $L$ is a language of bit strings
$L$ has a weak randomized verifier in the specified polynomial-time model
Its acceptance probability on members is at least $\min(2/3,(|x|+1)^{-c})$
It rejects every nonmember on every random string
